about: What the offline boot rig (.minecraft/dev/boot) prints that the live server does not. Read by icboot.py, which hands loud-check.ps1 the baseline of the tree under test PLUS this file. The live baseline (dev/loud/baseline.json) is never edited for the rig.
`signatures`: lines of a rig boot that are accepted, each with the reason it is a property of the rig (a fresh world, Linux, no players, loopback) and not of the tree under test.

`defects`: lines of a rig boot that are defects of the pack and that the live baseline does not carry under this wording. The same format and rule as the live baseline's (dev/loud/README.md): each with `count` and `family`; printed as recorded it is listed and is no finding, changed or grown it is one. The composed file takes the version of the tree's baseline, so an entry here needs both fields.
`liveness_skip`: entries of dev/loud/liveness_manifest.json that cannot print on the rig, each with the reason.

Same rules as the live baseline: nothing gets in without being read; a signature is the line without clock, numbers of two or more digits, addresses and ids, cut at 200 characters; no names, this file is public.

State on 2026-10-12 (pack 13a94cc4): of the live baseline's 160 accepted signatures the rig prints 154 (the six missing are the Patreon-library network failures, marked runtime there), and of its 9 defects it prints 7. README.md, section 'The rig against the live server', explains the two it does not print.

2026-10-24: the one defect listed here (the rig's wording of the cataclysm_ut:kill_monstrosity2 advancement line) was removed, as its entry asked, together with the live one: the G16 trim 7453b9da replaced that advancement with an empty copy, and the live entry was pruned in c4952b8c.
